Why the Democratic Party treated a lifelong Democrat as a threat -- threatened me with a lawsuit and jail time over a lie -- and what it taught me about the machine we're up against, & steps to fix it. | | | Jul 11 | | | | | | | | | | | | You would think a lifelong Democrat -- someone raised in this party, committed to its stated ideals of civil rights, working people, equality, justice, freedom, and the plain proposition that every person deserves a voice -- would be welcomed in the "big tent." That is not what happened to me. I don't especially want to talk about this. I would rather work on what our families need and what we can build together. But people keep asking me what happened during my last campaign -- why the establishment came after me, why a grassroots Democratic leader of a new generation got treated as a threat by her own party. So here's the answer, as plainly as I can give it. Context: I ran for Congress in 2024. Same seat. Same district. And what happened then tells us a lot about where we are as a country, what lies and misrepresentations prevent actual change, why we aren't where we need to be, and where the changes need to happen to structurally improve our politics: which I believe is, and should be, the exercise of power in service of responsibility and love for the people. | | ---|---|--- The party is not the people Call me crazy, but I believe the support of the people should be the only criterion for democratic legitimacy. Not whether insiders approve of you. Not whether the consultants find you convenient, or the major donors find you safe, or whether you'll accept the ideological and financial terms set by the people who already hold power. Just the people. That 's literally the whole point. If government "of the people, by the people, for the people" was good enough for Abraham Lincoln as he fought to bring this country back together after the Civil War, it ought to be good enough for the Democratic Party today. But here's the uncomfortable truth: America 's political parties are not public democratic institutions. Legally, they operate a lot more like private clubs -- and they'll tell you so, in open court, when it suits them. Remember 2016. Bernie Sanders ran an insurgent primary that caught fire -- and then, in its final stretch, thousands of internal DNC emails spilled into public view. They showed party officials, the very people who had sworn up and down they were neutral referees, privately disparaging the Sanders campaign and working to smooth Hillary Clinton's path to the nomination. The fallout was severe enough to force the DNC's chair to resign on the eve of the party's own convention. A group of Democratic voters and donors then sued the DNC over what those emails revealed -- the case is Wilding v. DNC Services Corp. Their claim was simple: the DNC's own charter promises that its officers will "maintain impartiality and evenhandedness" during the presidential nominating process, and the party had broken that promise. You know what the DNC's lawyers argued? That the promise didn 't really count. In open court, they characterized the charter's guarantee of impartiality as "political rhetoric" -- not a real obligation, not something a court could enforce. They said the party had every right, if it wanted, to let its insiders "go into back rooms like they used to and smoke cigars and pick the candidate that way." Read that again. The party that sells itself to America as the guardian of democracy stood up in federal court and argued that it was under no enforceable obligation to actually be democratic. Y'all. It makes me nauseous. To the country 's credit, the judge didn't buy the spin. He called it a "trivialization" of the DNC's own values and said the party had "committed itself to a higher principle." And then he dismissed the case anyway -- on the technicality that the voters couldn't prove they'd personally been defrauded. The practical message to every rank-and-file Democrat was the one the court spelled out: your redress is "through the ballot box... not through the judiciary." In other words: trust us, or leave. And if you're tempted to file this under "2016 was a long time ago" or "that's just sour grapes from the Bernie people" -- don't take my word for it. Take my opponent's. In July 2024, as the party was in convulsions over whether to keep Joe Biden on the presidential ticket, Congressman Adam Smith -- the 30-year incumbent I am running to unseat -- went on national television and said the quiet part out loud: "Joe Biden was not picked in 2020 because he was the only person that could beat Donald Trump. He was picked because he was the only person that could beat Bernie Sanders, rightly or wrongly."[2] Sit with that, because a sitting congressman just described his own party choosing its presidential nominee not by asking who could best serve the country, and not (heaven forbid!) by listening to the people! - but by asking who could best stop its own voters ' first choice. That wasn't a leak. It wasn't a hack. It wasn't me. That was the man who has held this seat for nearly thirty years, explaining on camera how the machine actually works -- and treating it as the most normal thing in the world. He wasn't "confessing" - he didn't think he was saying anything out of the ordinary. He was describing the water he swims in. (A necessary aside: I am not letting the Republican Party off the hook. Its escalating racism, its misogyny, its drift toward outright authoritarianism have been more than enough to keep me far away from it. I simply know the Democratic machinery more intimately -- it's the party I was raised in, the party my husband spent decades organizing inside, the one whose inner workings I've now experienced up close. This is not a story about Republicans being better. It's a story about one of America's only two political parties failing to be what it tells you it is.) Why would they come after me? Because I represent We the People, and I'm committed to being someone the machinery doesn't control. Because I won't take poison money from corporate, defense, and foreign interests that are against the interests of American communities, profit from our extraction, or benefit from destroying our sovereignty. Because I listen - with real empathy - to voices the insiders would rather manage, deride, or ignore. Because I don't believe disagreement is a threat to democracy -- I believe disagreement is democracy. Listening to people we don't agree with doesn't weaken a society. It's close to the only thing that has ever made one wiser. But a great deal of party structure isn't built for open deliberation. It's built to control the outcome while preserving the appearance of participation. Votes happen. Meetings are held. Committees conduct interviews. Members are allowed to speak. And yet the decisive questions are usually settled before any of that begins: Who gets to vote? Who appoints the deciders? Who controls the agenda and interprets the rules? Who gets the voter data, the donor lists, the consultants, the infrastructure that decide whether you're even considered "viable"? I've watched dedicated, principled party members subjected to something close to a public execution -- humiliated, stripped of their positions, driven out -- for the crime of being independent-minded. I've watched coordinated smear campaigns run against people who wouldn't fall in line. Myself included. | | ---|---|--- About that time they tried to kill my campaign When I ran in 2024, as a first-time, grassroots candidate answerable only to the people, I earned the endorsement of the Veterans and Military Families Caucus of the Washington State Democrats. (Side note: in earlier years, the State Dem party had tried to end the system of independent caucuses, because they weretoo independent, too vocal, making their own endorsements and representing the interests of their members. My husband lived through that phase of the Party -- he attended WA State Dems Executive Board meetings for eight years. Popular outcry saved the caucus structure. But that victory was won , it wasn't assured.) Winning that endorsement was a big deal for my campaign. Adam Smith, the incumbent I'm running against, is the Ranking Member (top Democrat) on the House Armed Services Committee, and he's held that position for decades. He has an enormous amount of political capital riding on his perceived representation of veterans and military families... but he has never served in the military, and no one in his family has either. Unlike me -- a Navy daughter, wife of a wheelchair-bound disabled Army veteran... -- and the caucus went for authentic affinity and genuine support of the people. That was a threat to Adam Smith, and the party's incumbent-protection system that he's embedded in. Naturally, I immediately started publicizing my endorsement. Running a grassroots campaign, early in the season, we didn't have a lot of money, and we put most of it into printed materials prominently featuring this vote of confidence, among many others. Then some days later, I got an email from the Washington State Democrats. In it was a letter from the most expensive law firm they have, asserting that I was falsely claiming the endorsement, that the meeting never happened, and threatening me with a lawsuit under RCW (Revised Code of Washington) 42.17A.335, which provides for penalties up to and including jail time. I was the pregnant mother of a toddler at the time, a emerging grassroots leader of their own party ... and out of the blue, they tried to kill my campaign and threatened me with jail time. I did nothing wrong. But here's the real kicker. They knew it was a lie. Here's how I know. Shasti Conrad is the Chair of the Washington State Democrats. She's the top Democratic Party official in the State of Washington. (Since 2024, she has also become Vice Chair of the Democratic National Committee - so now she's #2 in the entire nation.) Shasti - herself \- appointed an acting Chair for that particular meeting, at the 2024 WA State Dems Convention that June weekend in Seattle. That Acting Chair? A federal attorney named Nick Brown, who won his 2024 campaign and is now The Attorney General of the State of Washington , right up there at the top of those leading the legal challenges to the Trump Administration. He took the lead on the legal challenge to Trump's executive order stripping birthright citizenship, on behalf of Washington and a number of other states. He's about the most credible possible Chair of a caucus meeting you could have. Shasti appointed him as Acting Chair for that meeting. And then Shasti 's name is on the attorney's letter against me, which claims in black and white that the meeting never happened. Couldn't be any clearer: She knew. More than that: the Minutes from that meeting were sent to the Party Affairs director, as well as the Political Advisor Drew Estep, by the Vice-Chair (Joel Ware) within 48 hours of that meeting taking place: June 23rd, 2024. . But then - as the first step in their escalation, that same Senior Advisor Drew Estep emailed me, asserting that the Caucus "has not met this cycle" and that it was "not possible that your campaign has been endorsed by this Caucus." (Boldface emphasis in his letter. Evidence .) That email was sent on July 5th, 2024 - nearly two weeks after the Minutes had been emailed to Drew Estep directly. We have those Minutes from that meeting, showing the appointment of an acting Chair, showing all the normal conduct of meeting business, and confirming my endorsement. They're . I have the letter from the law firm, with Shasti's name on the cc line, asserting that "the meeting never happened," that I was falsely claiming the endorsement, and threatening me with a lawsuit and jail time unless I destroyed all my campaign materials that featured the endorsement and sent them proof within 24 hours , which amounted to tens of thousands of dollars - most of what we had. Read this letter yourself . In this particular case, we circulated our evidence, and they backed down. I never got to face them in court. But let me ask you: Wouldn 't you feel deeply hurt, disappointed, and betrayed? I don't share these facts lightly. I'm sharing it because you deserve to understand what an entrenched special interest and advisor within that institution addicted to its own power does when it meets a principled, strong, genuine candidate it can't buy, discipline, absorb, or comfortably control. I'm not complaining because it happened to me. I'm documenting , because if you're sincere, dedicated, and committed to justice, and you try to gain the power required to actually see justice done through one of the only pathways available - it will happen to you. Epstein was allowed to operate with impunity as long as he did, because the political bureaucracy was cowed, complicit, bought out, or actively supportive. If we don't deal with this , we're in for more of the same. How internal democracy gets engineered away I've sat through a lot of Democratic endorsement interviews, at the legislative-district and county level. I've won plenty -- and losing an endorsement is nobody's grievance; no candidate is owed one. The problem isn't the outcomes. It's the architecture underneath them. In a growing number of local party organizations (which are organized at the County level and the LD - Legislative Direct - level, below the State), the Chair personally appoints five or more members of the Executive Board. When a Board only seats eight or ten or twelve people, that means whichever faction wins the Chair can hand itself a governing majority by appointment -- not by a vote of the general body. Ordinary members can want a different direction by a mile and still be structurally locked out of ever electing a majority of the body that speaks in their name. The same trick runs through endorsements. The Chair or the Board appoints the committee that interviews candidates and decides who gets recommended. And if that committee declines to recommend a candidate, the membership often needs a supermajority -- 60%, sometimes two-thirds, I've even heard 70% -- just to overrule their own committee and endorse you directly. Sit with that a moment. A handful of people, chosen through a process the leadership already controls, can decline to recommend a grassroots candidate -- and then that candidate has to clear a supermajority of the entire room simply to undo one gatekeeping decision. Let me tell you how hard it is to win two-thirds of a political organization as a newcomer who won't play the transactional game power demands - especially when, in a Congressional race, I have eleven LDs to seek endorsement from. Now I 've done it, more than once. But the field is nowhere close to level. In 2024, the 48th LD overcame a committee recommendation against, and endorsed me - a grassroots challenger of an entrenched incumbent - by a 2:1 ratio. The 33rd LD, Adam Smith's home district, where he grew up and went to high school - they disavowed him and endorsed me. In fact, they were the very first to do so. The 31st LD, down in rural Auburn, rescinded their endorsement of Adam Smith and endorsed me. The 43rd LD Democrats, dense central Seattle, arguably the most powerful in the State of Washington, formally censured Adam Smith and endorsed me. (Smith had been making the rounds on TV calling the grassroots protestors for peace and justice and an end to genocide, "left wing authoritarians" and calling for their, and our, arrest and jail time. That type of anti-First Amendment rhetoric has NO place in our politics, especially from someone who claims to represent the People, and identifies with the "Democratic" Party.) This year, the structures have been tightened: among the few LDs that don't have a committee hurdle to clear (where endorsements are voted on directly by the members) many now require a 60% threshold for endorsement, not a simple majority. In two LDs this year, I have missed the endorsement threshold by 1 vote. In one case, I won 59.57% of the vote... and despite winning a clear majority and being less than half a percent below their stated endorsement threshold, I did not formally receive that body's endorsement. It would be maddening, but it's not surprising anymore. Over the past two years, I've watched these structures tighten, not loosen -- particularly after the surge of grassroots energy in 2024 over genocide and the slaughter of innocent children on our taxpayer dime, and the conduct of Democratic officials. That is not healthy internal disagreement. That's consolidation. | | ---|---|--- "Viability" is manufactured Then there's everything that happens outside the endorsement room -- because the Party doesn't just hand out a symbolic blessing. It controls access to the machinery you need to run at all. The detailed voter file alone can run tens of thousands of dollars. A professional treasurer familiar with federal compliance regulations -- expensive also. Consultants, tens of thousands each -- and they don't just sell you a service, they function as gatekeepers , the toll booths between you and the donors, the power players, the endorsers, the operatives, the friendly press. They also become security and intelligence vulnerabilities inside your own campaign, and, in my honest opinion, a great deal of the money spent on them is simply wasted. Add polling, digital, advertising, mail, printing, canvassing, text banking, field, compliance -- and a serious Congressional race becomes a seven-figure enterprise fast. For someone just starting out, accessing voter data for free from the Party is a major gate. If you can clear that hurdle, you have a chance. If you don't, you may not. It's as simple as that. Party support also provides access to software to run your campaign, free of charge (rather than thousands per month). It also gives you a small army of volunteers... PCOs and other local party members who cheerfully spend their summers canvassing for whoever their LD endorsed. Here in Washington State, I was told that access to the Party's voter file and NGPVan, the main outreach software, was contingent on winning endorsement from over 50% of the LDs within my Congressional district. (Eleven, in my case.) I had to win 6. I won 4. Against every structural impediment thrown in my way... coming into politics out of nowhere, I won four. If nothing else, that 's proof that even inside the Party structure, people wereand arehungry for real representation. But without clearing that threshold, I was locked out of Party infrastructure. So I ran a pedal-to-the-metal grassroots campaign primarily focused on physical outreach: flyers, banners, yard signs, canvassing - inescapable visibility that couldn't be throttled by digital data, deplatformed or shadowbanned online due to my principles, or infiltrated by other campaigns. And I won over 90,000 votes. Here's what I learned: Politics in America is an industry. A giant economic flywheel of polling, printing, advertising, and consulting - much of it sheer manipulation - fueled by hope and fear and pain and carefully managed narrative. And it is very good at taking brave, decent people and teaching them that survival means becoming part of the machine they came to improve. Take money from the approved donors. Hire the approved people. Repeat the approved language. Don't challenge the incumbents the party has decided to protect. Don't ask where the money comes from. Don't get unpredictable. I'm what that machine chokes on. Incumbency has become a guarantee All of this matters because the United States has built one of the most powerful systems of incumbent protection in the democratic world. In recent Congressional elections, House incumbents who run for reelection win around 95% of the time. Or more. That's not just a healthy advantage of experience and name recognition. That's a near-guarantee. Safe seats, gerrymandered maps to keep the incumbent (or at least the same party) in power over decades, single-member districts decided in low-turnout primaries, decades-deep donor relationships, and a press that treats incumbents as the default and challengers as curiosities -- the advantages stack on advantages until the election is competitive in form and settled in fact. Without the party's backing, or a coordinated retirement in which leadership decides it's finally time to open a seat (to whomever they approve...), a challenger faces very long odds. Which means the Party gets to decide who's "viable." It can quietly require you to accept a particular line, a particular funding model, a particular set of loyalties -- not to mention, particular entrenched advisors who've come from the Party itself. (The revolving door is real, at all levels.) Toe the line, and the blessings of praise, support, and access to power are showered upon you. Refuse, and you're thrown to the wolves. That's what happened to me. Healthier democracies aren't like this. Incumbency still helps in them -- experience should count for something -- but across comparable Western parliaments, incumbent reelection rates tend to run closer to 70%. Not like ours, at 95%+. The distance between "a real advantage" and "a near-lock" is the distance between a genuine competitive democracy and what political scientists have called congressional stagnation : a system that holds individual officeholders in place at rates that look less like representation and more like fiefdoms -- even as the public's approval of Congress sits in the basement. | | ---|---|--- This is how a government grows old and stops working You can see the cost in the age and condition of Congress itself. The average member of the House is now approaching 60. The average senator is in his or her mid-60s -- right around the age the rest of the country calls retirement. And those are averages. Roughly two dozen members of Congress are 80 or older. More than half the Senate is over 60. A handful of Senators are in their 80s, including one who's been MIA for weeks now, and one - an active, sitting Senator, Chuck Grassley, is in his 90s. In most functioning legislatures around the world, lawmakers run about 8-10 years older than the average of the people they serve. In ours, that gap is closer to 18-20 years. There is nothing wrong with an older person serving. Age brings memory, judgment, and hard-won wisdom, and I want all of that in our government. The problem isn't that elders serve. The problem is a system with so little turnover that people are pressured to stay -- long past the point a healthy institution would have raised up successors -- because there's no dignified path out, and no one waiting to take the baton who was ever allowed to. Colloquially speaking, our politics eats its own young. And so the baton gets passed the hardest way there is. Since 2016, 21 Senators and Representatives have died in office. 14 of them were Democrats. That is not an indictment of any one of those individuals necessarily; many were extraordinary public servants, and I mourn them. It is an indictment of a political culture that has forgotten how to let go. Look at what's happening even as I write this. One of the most powerful men in the Senate has been hospitalized for weeks under circumstances his own office won't explain -- to the point that his home-state Governor has had to publicly demand basic information about whether the people of that state are being represented at all. Whatever you think of his politics, and you know what I think of them, no Constitutional Republic should run this way. A seat in Congress is not a possession to be held tightly until your last breath. It is a public trust, lent by the people, meant to be handed on in turn. That is what a healthy government and party system would understand. Instead, too often, ours behaves like a ratchet. Republicans drag the country right; keep it from moving meaningfully back; and the machinery locks the result in place and calls it pragmatism. That's how a country destroys its own future. That's how political imagination dies. That's how people stop believing the whole system can ever answer them again. What we can actually change The single most direct fix is congressional term limits. I support a hard cap -- 12 years in the House, 18 in the Senate. Long enough to build real expertise, real relationships, and a real record. Not long enough to turn a public office into private property. Term limits guarantee the openings that let new leaders rise, they keep advantage from compounding forever, and they force the parties to develop successors instead of protecting incumbents until scandal or death does the job for them. Term limits alone won't do it, though. We also need independent redistricting , so voters pick their representatives instead of representatives picking their voters. Ranked-choice voting, so people can vote their conscience without being trapped by "spoilers." Public campaign financing and equal, affordable access to voter data, so a good candidate with no rich friends can still reach the people, make their case, and offer their service. And inside the parties themselves: legal accountability, transparent bylaws, governing boards elected directly by the membership, strict limits on appointed seats, lower thresholds for members to overrule their own committees, real protection for caucuses and dissenting voices, and open records for endorsement votes and internal discipline. The answer, I believe, is not to burn political organization down. Parties, at their best, are how people gather, deliberate, teach one another, recruit candidates, build coalitions, and turn shared values into governing power. That's the reason we built them. The answer is to make them belong to the people again. | | ---|---|--- What I still believe I believe in democracy. Not the branding. Not the ceremonies. Not the carefully managed performance of participation -- the real thing. People thinking together. People disagreeing honestly. People coming to agreement where they can, and genuinely competing fairly in public when they cannot. People choosing who represents them, and removing them when they stop serving the public's interest. People handing knowledge and responsibility from one generation to the next, on purpose, with grace. Government of the people, by the people, and for the people. That should not be a radical demand inside the Democratic Party. It should be the minimum requirement for using the name. Care. Courage. # George Washington Won With
Maryland's 400.

Now, let's remember them and fight for Maryland's future.
Dear ,
You've heard the story. 400 brave Maryland soldiers of the First Maryland Regiment under Major Gist heroically stood their ground at the Old Stone House in Brooklyn buying General George Washington and 9,000 Continental troops precious time to escape across the East River, thereby saving the American War for Independence in its infancy.

The Maryland 400 held the line - later earning our State the nickname by General Washington as the "Old Line State."

And I need you to be part of our ["Maryland 400" team now](https://us.list-manage.com/zjhBgucdJ1P?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b).

I am asking you to stop what you are doing and help us hold the line once again. Democratic Socialists, whom Governor Moore has praised, are seeking to use Maryland and your tax dollars to advance their attack on our State and Nation.

The Republican Governor's Association has stepped up to endorse and help us. However, we need to raise a war chest NOW.

**We are launching the "Maryland 400" to stand once again as the Old Line State.** I am asking 400 Marylanders to join by each [donating $2500](https://us.list-manage.com/UEA5OGoR8rf?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) to help us reach our initial goal to beat Wes Moore and save Maryland.

If you cannot be part of our Maryland 400, then for our 250th anniversary of this Nation, would you chip in $250? If everyone on this e-mail list donated even just $100 we would have what we need to hold the line and win against Wes Moore and his tax and spend, high fees, high cost of living plans for you and me and our State.

This is a timely request. We only have 30 days to do this and show those that want to help us that we are ready for the fight and bringing it together. Please donate today and be part of history - remember the Maryland 400.

Thank you,

Dan Cox
Republican Nominee for Governor

Authority: Dan Cox for Governor; Nick Krop, CPA, Treasurer.

| | Dear Friend,

In the spring of 1775, a handful of farmers and tradesmen stood their ground against the greatest military power on earth.

They didn’t know how the story would end.

But they knew that freedom was worth fighting for.

The “shot heard ’round the world” set in motion a chain of events that led to the greatest experiment in self-government the world has ever known.

That’s why I’m excited to share something special with you.

**The White House recently asked Hillsdale College to assist the Salute to America 250 Task Force in producing a new free video series, [_The Story of America_](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.aaeXzEt0C1CqCJbIn3CZe191H17ij8Nn2XfXlCLy55sOwqmrPEirGfKvcgaCD1Qq-pp84Q5rOnFztn4h9vGF8ct_LLzn62xPaxAXEMZWXGsxMgqCWOU8nkPWuzNmFvMNwG3gHYFN6I-85GeFmtcH7hYdemknSwTARFNEG5DrtPIFJ-aenMi_9IdiAVJZAiqn4UFXZAbKcBrrvkfsELV8q81sobWTDHLF3WbJsrxUNuh30ofkjBYhc2Sk3ly935dIEWbdRCNE6CMYCFMsO4feI88Y8lgh0-Hjq_wGkoJToauCG5DczF5Miv_xQM2cpmHe/4s8/SFL88QTgRlG0Ajy-RgjweQ/h2/h001.GnvRe4Hj2Pf86PzdrTY0aia9ZOlP30or_1fc6_Qsnko)** —a sweeping, episode-by-episode journey through our nation’s founding in honor of its 250th anniversary.

As we approach the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, this series invites you to learn about the principles, courage, sacrifice, and faith that made America possible—and _why this story still matters today_.

Filmed in the historic Indian Treaty Room in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building in Washington, D.C., each episode brings a pivotal chapter of the American story to life.

**Here’s a glimpse of what you can access on your journey at no cost:****
**

* **The Declaration of Independence** — _Larry P. Arnn, President, Hillsdale College_
How the Declaration of Independence defines who we are—and what it still asks of us

* **The Formation of the Army** — _Pete Hegseth, Secretary of War_
The moment citizen-patriots took up arms and answered liberty’s call against overwhelming odds

* **The King’s Call to Arms** — _U.S. Senator Mike Lee_
When imperial authority collided with colonial defiance—and compromise was no longer possible

* **The Culper Spy Ring** — _Brian Kilmeade, Co-Author, George Washington’s Secret Six_
The remarkable story of ordinary Americans who risked everything to outsmart the British and save the Revolution

* **Story of the American Soldier** — _Michael Knowles, Author and Podcaster_
A tribute to the forgotten men whose sacrifice secured American independence

* **The U.S. Marine Corps Birthday** — _Vice President J.D. Vance_
The enduring legacy of courage, service, and sacrifice that defines the U.S. Marine Corps

**You can receive instant access to this free video series right now using this secure link: **

**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/story-of-america-free-access](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.aaeXzEt0C1CqCJbIn3CZe191H17ij8Nn2XfXlCLy55sOwqmrPEirGfKvcgaCD1Qq-pp84Q5rOnFztn4h9vGF8ct_LLzn62xPaxAXEMZWXGsxMgqCWOU8nkPWuzNmFvMNwG3gHYFN6I-85GeFmtcH7hYdemknSwTARFNEG5DrtPIFJ-aenMi_9IdiAVJZAiqn4UFXZAbKcBrrvkfsELV8q81sobWTDHLF3WbJsrxUNuh30ofkjBYhc2Sk3ly935dI8UE8nrs6jBHBQT54h9p-lk6U1z9KYB9syjktW3U4I74hLwYhnPJB2fyJVbs3L2i2/4s8/SFL88QTgRlG0Ajy-RgjweQ/h3/h001.KU5HpznFdrewXgC3aSwSUklgoMdvJtmxx0_UjqT9Gek)**

**As we approach our nation’s 250th anniversary, now is the time to rediscover the spirit of 1776.**

And it’s my hope that, by remembering the great deeds of the past, we can inspire Americans today to equally great deeds.

Enjoy your free video series!

Bill Gray ’01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

**P.S.** New episodes will be released throughout the year as we approach America’s 250th anniversary—sign up now so you don’t miss a single one!

## Military Bases Pump $148.8B Into Texas
Republican Gov. Greg Abbott [announced Friday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3uozAQR09jOkceQzAULrah-2-7JfLHQCwNdoQnJLn9Coq9wPbznt78_vzMPy5Ryutvt6Hlz1LmjO9KyIz7zPhx1RFVdnvN-Pb0Qo9Ey6yV7qUyEmCOLtF37ppovYojNGjBDK3pTT8OzcPG0JsF-rYNMeBd66VVAAGCH4O6tzg0yZ4yZQAAFLRwM-quYdCjGTB2xo-iUxgTl_3GD7ySFvqWA_dbKFtD9sH8rKL9JfQk9FRddnlFKpQOPC-Ens6XhJ4uVujpX7wSelrLIZ33hVm6nMsrB6wSumGQPhGlkiWGksuWgkzb0wWWW6LEbv_KlCs7Isep5Cove7Pb-HyfYO2N6NS6uURXJ__fuofVfwMAAP__fdWQZg) that U.S. military installations contribute an estimated $148.8 billion a year to the Texas economy, supporting 628,884 direct and indirect jobs statewide. The comptroller's biennial study, produced with the Texas Military Preparedness Commission, found the state's 14 installations also generated [$91.4 billion](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uqzAQhJ8GOiPb_BgKF7ehy21PiWxYJystdmRvQnj7o_AKpxxpZvTN_NyWm0PCeP_vdrD8CWmJcBQCZsgLw8cVR1TY5RLh8PQCD0Rh0VIPQhqh1LI5pHPp6s16uU2qBqvM2JrBDNNYPy4R1jYMZp00dKDl1PfBh1GPg-qHtkb7LZNGKaWkalVjZK_VqCczwtYZP1WdhA055YYfcCEFOtMbcrOmvSb7YH6Wqv1X6bnS83EcTUgf416FMX4tlZ6_myo9X2GxIyG7fAqMhR2RY0yxiDVFzuhfDEJ1oxeFHUMRsKaY9lNkeKbMoriz1NluzwOJsAym6uR9d0gXDP_twrfVvwEAAP__0eaIog) in gross domestic product. Joint Base San Antonio leads at $53.5 billion in output, with Fort Hood [second at $37.9 billion](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAUhZ8GOwygI1JQ_I3d_O2WBoerkr3CBO4OM2-_0VfY5jQn58uX83Wf7y5giNt_d4Cl95rmCLUgEEGeCd6uOMRCLpcIdcEfWABxnZVQAxeaSzl7F_Az9423i_BGNmClHjs96MGMzW6VHtWgwZnVDBKg7_zNGGHGxXjtXOebYE-Y0FJKKWQnWy1uSo7K6BF8rxfDegE-UMot7XAprfhJL8jtIx0N2p3oWVj3j6mJqanW2n5Xep8lU9PJZmoS-gzF1LSmTHxPyfMMhwux8BSBX1i-hG2DQvwIGMjlD4dHiukIDw5xCxEKz_A892VPtTA1Ndn6Zw2IoQya9WI7XMBLi_525suq3wAAAP__kCOJnA) and Fort Bliss third at $29.1 billion. "_The tradition of military service is long in our great state_ ," Abbott said, adding that each base "_serves as a major local employer_."
## Texas Sends Six to MLB All-Star Weekend
Six players with ties to Texas clubs [will take the field](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAUhJ8Gd1j82GAXFNu4y7ZbWhAOMdpjYwEJydtfxa9w-9E3882_23qzEePx-Gt3MPUd0npAKwi1Ql4rvG2xiKXaXA5oDp_gADGsgglFmaacr95G_KxD541jfuYdGK4nqZVW89RtRjs7egXMSXnnYQh-mu9OD2GUclZejl00XxjTnHPOuOS9ZqPgk5j1BH7QbiYDAx9ryn3d4JoU8JNekPt72js0W61nIfIPEQsRS2utD-kt1JaepabjGyJiKWfKtRCxXAB6ov1ALvTy2NFRi0i_mrQB_IfDd9n4s0XEWJQmA3vsNuJVWH9308uInwAAAP__YER9WQ) at MLB All-Star Weekend in Philadelphia, culminating in Tuesday's 96th All-Star Game at Citizens Bank Park. Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez, who leads the majors in OPS and the American League in home runs, was [voted the starter](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOszAQBeDTmA7kMQSbwsXf0OVvt0TjeEgsDTiyvXGyp1_BFbYead773td1uWLgsN__40a2vNe47FQzUymUlkJvzMicC6a8U3X8TY6Y10VJNbZStwCLx8CfZWi8ddJP0JAFbXo96nEyzcOivF1c70bqycjB9UhOGu1HgwCXafVNsMczqQEAJPTQaXlRYNSkDflBu0kMknwoMXXlQWellT_xRam7xa1h-yjlmUX_T6hZqLnW2m3sjptQM-aSYhZqPlRCzZ-YPO4t8gsT_bQ7buTbE4PM7eFskvXPGphDHrUY5H3DwGdS-ds-L6t-AwAA___FY3pO) at designated hitter, his fourth selection; Rangers reliever Jacob Latz was [also named](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2S4yAQhJ8GZbgAYYECgkuU-dILVYMY2VyNhAtm_bNPvyW_wsZd1d3f9-8yXyBT3q9_YcPAr7XMOz4bITPWmfEFDYgaQ207PiN9YUSidTbKDFI5qfWcINN7tl0KUaVRdxi0870b3DD67hbOBl30KkXnln5ZcPS2H85xdX3yUdu1y-EoU05rrZXu9cmps9HejM5jsi6OwipMmUs98Q0_l1Z6lwfW01K2jsKN-d5E_0eYSZhpLS97IByhMFO7l8pNmKnCfsXa5H9YSpQE_C132DDJjaIEInlASkbYuhrS_ZmJchucsOq6QabPFv_O0COYnwAAAP__F4h79w) to the AL squad. Four prospects play Sunday's Futures Game: San Antonio Missions catcher Ethan Salas, Midland RockHounds pitcher Jamie Arnold and infielder Leo De Vries, and Rangers farmhand Caden Scarborough. The Home Run Derby follows Monday.
## World Cup Smashes Arlington Hotel Record
Arlington's hotels and short-term rentals pulled in a [record $31 million](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OrSAURp8GOwxsOaIFxW3s5ra3NPxslWQrBjjDzNvfOK8w9Zd8WWv9-1g_bKR47X_tiaZ-bWm9sBXCWjGvFb9ssUSl2lwubI7e6JBoW0HAyIXmUq7BRvpeVReME2GWHRqpp0GPepyn7jBynoVVOE1KwaDkyyGIlwYPwyZGv7kumudMaCmlFHKQvRYvkBPMesKgtJuZEhhiTbmvB_4gbfSdPjH3Pp0dmaPWu7DhD4OFwdJa6y_nw9aemcHy-DBYKHlLDBabH92aLu6R0GVbsfCMPuXAa3rnWE6-U3KWeLlTpbgfldvCW8oUuH_f_EKbC9_iZQkZLEqocZwGBkuXTbhbJIpl1EyJ_bSRfiDr79J-GvgfAAD__9ALjuM) in June as the city hosted FIFA World Cup matches, officials said. clean_body: The same man I married is the exact same one serving in Congress today. | Peter, There are three things my husband, Tim Burchett, has never lacked: I've spent enough years married to him to know that once he gets an idea in his head, there is absolutely no changing it. Believe me, I've tried. The funny thing is, that same hardheaded streak is exactly why so many people support him. When Tim sees something that isn't right, he speaks up. When he thinks taxpayers are getting taken for a ride, he says so. And when somebody in Washington tells him to sit down, be quiet, and go along with the crowd, that's usually when he gets even louder. That's one reason I've never worried much about Washington changing him. | | He's never cared much about the perks or the titles. While plenty of politicians settle into the Washington lifestyle, Tim still sleeps in his office. He'd rather save taxpayers a few dollars than spend them trying to impress somebody. With the midterm elections only a few months away, we know what's coming. The attacks will get louder. The special interests will spend millions. And the Washington crowd would love nothing more than to replace independent voices like Tim with people who know how to keep their heads down and fall in line. That has never been Tim's strong suit. He's going to keep fighting for East Tennessee, for common sense, and for the values that brought so many of us together in the first place. | Thank you for everything you do for our family and for our campaign. Think our voting machines are un-hackable? Let me show you how to flip a vote! | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/rachelhamm/i-can-flip-votes?e=5fa0631807)
---
| |

| Dear Patriots, I just released a must-watch new video that cuts through the noise on election security — and it’s one of the most important ones I’ve put out yet. In this video, I break down exactly what the **Save America Act** is doing to secure our elections... and what it is **not** doing. I lay out the facts so you can separate truth from spin. Then, I'm going to show you a video of my friend **Mark Cook** in a jaw-dropping presentation. He shows — step by step — exactly how he can hack voting machines and flip votes in real time. This isn’t theory. This is a clear demonstration of the vulnerabilities that exist in our current systems. I also touch on the **California election system** , including the troubling details of what happened with **Spencer Pratt’s** election. If you want to understand how these systems actually operate — and where they fail — this show is essential viewing. **Watch the show here:**
YouTube: [https://youtu.be/1s6iVQ3X950?si=63E98XubCwhJ0upB](https://us.list-manage.com/1BtOP7fp4D6?e=5fa0631807&c2id=f026e449d203fb75a1e6e9f9d310f4bc)
Rumble: [https://rumble.com/v7ci9oq-episode-78-video-proof-of-how-election-machines-can-be-hacked.html](https://us.list-manage.com/jMeGkbi8Gd3?e=5fa0631807&c2id=f026e449d203fb75a1e6e9f9d310f4bc)
(YouTube is throttling this video because of the controversial content. They don't want you to see how votes can be flipped!!) Our elections are the foundation of this great republic. At the end of the day, the message is clear: **If we don’t completely eliminate all voting machines, our country is facing a major national security risk.** Bad actors — both foreign and domestic — have the ability to manipulate our elections, and the evidence is impossible to ignore. Please watch the video, share it with your friends and family, and help spread the word. The time for real election integrity is now. Please contact your reps to let them know that election integrity is at the top of your list for things they need to work on!
---

body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair
---
The Enemy Within - Communism
As we read almost daily about Communists, or their alias "progressive socialists", who among us could imagine that we would face this threat to our government and way of life here in Nebraska. This definitely wouldn't have been on my bingo card five years ago. We have seen over the last several years that the Democrat Party has swung more and more to the left; this is the result.
Here in Nebraska we have two Democrat Socialists of America chapters, one in Lincoln and one in Omaha. What was touted as socialism has made its natural evolution into Communism as evidenced in states such as New York, Colorado, Maine, and Montana, with additional activity in states like Michigan, Florida, California, Oregon, Arizona, Georgia, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Vermont, Utah, Maryland, Texas, and yes, here in Nebraska.
The Democrat Party of our parents' and grandparents' day is not the Democrat Party of today and their party is being taken over from within. Two new offshoots of the Democrat Party are being formed in Nebraska as we speak - The Nebraska Working Families Party and the America First Party. There are two reasons or this: one is that these parties want to be the vanguard for a more rapid decline/takeover of the rabid left of the Nebraska Democrat Party. Two is that the recent SCOTUS ruling that removed limits for State Parties to directly coordinate with federal candidates.
Each Political Party can accept $10,000 per individual and use that money in coordination with federal candidates. The NEGOP will be following closely who funds these new parties and who benefits from them. If you have three parties supporting one candidate, that would be $30,000 from each individual donor and thus amplify the money that candidate can receive from a single source.
We are under threat in Nebraska from posers who want to wear the mantle of non-partisan like Dan Osborn (against Senator Pete Ricketts), Austin Ahlman (against Congressman Mike Flood), and Brent Comstock (against Regent candidate Jeremy Hosein). I would also include "Dark Money Denise Powell (running against CD2 candidate Brinker Harding) in this group.
Fortunately, more moderate Democrats saw the radical leftist leanings of Kara Eastman and Tony Vargas and helped to keep Congressman Don Bacon in office. We can only hope that they will do so again.
Many of our party are still sleepwalking through elections and don't see that we have an existential threat to our way of life here in Nebraska. The NEGOP will do its best to keep the spotlight on this threat, but it will take all of us to work together against it.
The Republican Party has had poor turnout in recent elections and we cannot allow that to happen again. Not showing up to vote is silent consent to the radical communist takeover of our state. I do not exaggerate. As the adage goes, "You can vote yourself into Communism, but you have to shoot your way out of Communism".
Those of us in the NEGOP are working together to do our part to stave off the threat, but it will take all of us educating our families, friends, and neighbors to what is going on. We are fighting an enemy that seeks power by any means under the guise of "equality" or "justice". What they don't say is that they are fighting to make us all equally poor and equally yoked to a ruling class.
Consider this a challenge to all who read this message. We are the vanguard.
Credit: Virgil Walker (co-host, Just Thinking podcast) -- [read more on his Substack](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yPgpnce7QaD3Zi5L6pfFCM64SzKS1TNUPemWQvp1tnR-2B1KJkPSqCbdXeKBtMk09f-LetqKFIHKcF8P_8ePoxHgqhJJrtnBWuiUvcdgm1NAAnSdwze3a5n3RVTdBdiIcUxqu56Eu9vs0M4bmZv15jz2T8-tzeKcsARW6LuNz-Q=&c=-7XRXBfvAea9RIAe-aVyoVkjUz92U9-EObU2cdMmYouw1RKDeNumjw==&ch=fXwOMlfcWhS3pNo5td0Y1u9jvKf4_JxMPrGnbueMEcyBSIESd8cLSg==).

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair The Enemy Within - Communism As we read almost daily about Communists, or their alias "progressive socialists", who among us could imagine that we would face this threat to our government and way of life here in Nebraska. This definitely wouldn't have been on my bingo card five years ago. We have seen over the last several years that the Democrat Party has swung more and more to the left; this is the result. Here in Nebraska we have two Democrat Socialists of America chapters, one in Lincoln and one in Omaha. What was touted as socialism has made its natural evolution into Communism as evidenced in states such as New York, Colorado, Maine, and Montana, with additional activity in states like Michigan, Florida, California, Oregon, Arizona, Georgia, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Vermont, Utah, Maryland, Texas, and yes, here in Nebraska. The Democrat Party of our parents' and grandparents' day is not the Democrat Party of today and their party is being taken over from within. Two new offshoots of the Democrat Party are being formed in Nebraska as we speak - The Nebraska Working Families Party and the America First Party. There are two reasons or this: one is that these parties want to be the vanguard for a more rapid decline/takeover of the rabid left of the Nebraska Democrat Party. Two is that the recent SCOTUS ruling that removed limits for State Parties to directly coordinate with federal candidates. Each Political Party can accept $10,000 per individual and use that money in coordination with federal candidates. The NEGOP will be following closely who funds these new parties and who benefits from them. If you have three parties supporting one candidate, that would be $30,000 from each individual donor and thus amplify the money that candidate can receive from a single source. We are under threat in Nebraska from posers who want to wear the mantle of non-partisan like Dan Osborn (against Senator Pete Ricketts), Austin Ahlman (against Congressman Mike Flood), and Brent Comstock (against Regent candidate Jeremy Hosein). I would also include "Dark Money Denise Powell (running against CD2 candidate Brinker Harding) in this group. Fortunately, more moderate Democrats saw the radical leftist leanings of Kara Eastman and Tony Vargas and helped to keep Congressman Don Bacon in office. We can only hope that they will do so again. Many of our party are still sleepwalking through elections and don't see that we have an existential threat to our way of life here in Nebraska. The NEGOP will do its best to keep the spotlight on this threat, but it will take all of us to work together against it. The Republican Party has had poor turnout in recent elections and we cannot allow that to happen again. Not showing up to vote is silent consent to the radical communist takeover of our state. I do not exaggerate. As the adage goes, "You can vote yourself into Communism, but you have to shoot your way out of Communism". Those of us in the NEGOP are working together to do our part to stave off the threat, but it will take all of us educating our families, friends, and neighbors to what is going on. We are fighting an enemy that seeks power by any means under the guise of "equality" or "justice". What they don't say is that they are fighting to make us all equally poor and equally yoked to a ruling class. Consider this a challenge to all who read this message. We are the vanguard. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: What's Mississippi's Energy Advantage Worth to You?
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/july4th-12854011?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
The Magnolia State is booming. Since Tate Reeves became governor, more than $40 billion of investment has poured in — and hardly a week goes by without news of another mega deal.

This week brought fresh proof: Mississippi now ranks third in the entire nation for jobs created through reshoring and foreign investment — behind only Texas and South Carolina, and up from seventh just a year ago. First-quarter figures point to more than 12,000 new jobs from companies bringing production back to America and choosing to bring it right here. ([Read the story here.](https://us.list-manage.com/Emu5SSbAQes?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3))

So why are all these industries flocking in?

One key factor is energy — affordable, reliable energy. Data centers, factories and chemical plants shop for cheap, dependable power, and Mississippi has it.

Cheap, reliable energy is one of our greatest economic assets — and I want you to see exactly what it is worth to your own household. So, we built a new webtool: [**CompareMyPower.com**](https://us.list-manage.com/1AXkmX3KzUo?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3). Put in your ZIP code and a few details about your home, and it shows what you pay and what you would pay in a different state. Click on the image below to try it!
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/AR8u5hhAX9X?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)
---
| Try it — the findings are striking:
* Mississippi runs at about 16.8¢ a kilowatt-hour against 18.8¢ nationally, and barely half of California's 35.3¢.
* Almost every dollar on your Mississippi bill still buys actual electricity — generation and delivery — not a stack of subsidy schemes and program surcharges.

We only have to look at California — and across the Atlantic at Europe — to see where the wrong road ends. Britain, my native country, now has energy costs three to four times higher than America's, thanks to policies that restrict oil and gas drilling, ban shale gas and push heavily on intermittent wind and solar.

Britain has been overtaken by Mississippi in output per person. California made the same mistakes — cap-and-trade, forced retirements of reliable power plants, mandate piled on mandate — and its families pay for it every single month.

The lesson is simple: an energy advantage is easy to lose and hard to win back. Our job now is to protect cheap, reliable power, welcome new generation, and refuse to copy the mandates that made California and Britain so expensive.

Protect it, and we keep winning the data centers, the factories and the jobs. Follow California down the mandate road, and we throw it away.

As always, thank you for standing with us at the Mississippi Center for Public Policy as we work to promote freedom, prosperity, and sound policy here in our state.

Have a wonderful weekend!

Hi, Peter – How are you doing? There's a lot going on out there. The constant chaos in the federal government ranges from heartbreaking to infuriating. But as I travel our incredible state, I'm buoyed by your stories and support – and I'm more inspired than ever to deliver results for Vermont. Fortunately, I have a track record of producing big positive change in our state. I took a problem that everyone said was unsolvable and unfixable, and we went door to door and fixed it. I brought together Democrats, Republicans, and Progressives; I brought together families and businesses, and we actually made something better. And I have a plan to do it again. Lots of plans, actually. Together, they make up my platform, and I want to introduce each piece of **[my platform](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135066270/633007347/-750528621?refcode=ea.d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDc0ZmY5NmItMjg3ZC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=KYotQJALv0I_OAUM10SIWlUTJkENrgUSjT_gDWLQmtA=&emci=674f24c7-9e7c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378)** to you over the next few weeks. **Today, we'll start with the issue I see as a root cause of so many other challenges facing our state: Housing.** | [**READ MY PLATFORM**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135066271/633007348/-750528621?refcode=ea.d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDc0ZmY5NmItMjg3ZC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=KYotQJALv0I_OAUM10SIWlUTJkENrgUSjT_gDWLQmtA=&emci=674f24c7-9e7c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378)
---
Housing is _the key_ to unlocking our potential here in Vermont. Why?
Well, with more housing, we attract more families, which means we attract the workforce that makes our state run. That means we increase our tax base, and _that_ means we all pay less to live in the state that we love, and we have more resources to invest in our state, and all of us who want to live here can thrive.
So, how do we get there?
**We already know what works. We just need to supercharge it.[My plan](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135066272/633007349/-750528621?refcode=ea.d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDc0ZmY5NmItMjg3ZC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=KYotQJALv0I_OAUM10SIWlUTJkENrgUSjT_gDWLQmtA=&emci=674f24c7-9e7c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378) will:**
👉 Set regional building targets
👉 Establish a sales tax holiday on building supplies
👉 Implement a tax on second homes
👉 Provide templates for local and municipal zoning
👉 Build the workforce to build the homes
[**READ MY PLATFORM**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135066273/633007350/-750528621?refcode=ea.d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDc0ZmY5NmItMjg3ZC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=KYotQJALv0I_OAUM10SIWlUTJkENrgUSjT_gDWLQmtA=&emci=674f24c7-9e7c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=d74ff96b-287d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378)

I truly believe that the solutions to our biggest, most pressing challenges are within our reach. It's going to take vision, persistence, and collaboration to get there.
Let’s build Vermont together!

Democrats turned California into a cautionary tale. Florida is their next target — and we need your help to stop them. |
---

Patriot,

You know what California used to be?

**Sunny. Prosperous. Free.**

And then Democrats got hold of it.

[
](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=da70678d4d954b22bf04d05dc0d94457&_e=pUQuMl4WOsc59IER2eFenTUR70Djpl93VvQBdyERh5HLHnWDqO8FEl8VCQQfjmxbmnnFMV2ghW4aBFO7TNnJE39J9UbmA7oI0Fxt_VM9yd74VOT30Hv2ttlV7wMaqEZBPb_qqvf-QEVwlugdV7ixKfnsT_-UedfAWM4ZNMxK0-zcMFfcfSoY6HHc2uD5bKhQmZCer-5HbKa5VzbnoMfCHjl54xbuLvIHCueny16o1Ya05O_zZcHopskCqEIpHNHjX4YedECAH_lZhN_NSb-WcEptVBgmtohdqki0T8Z5Hry4c-WWz32SBzKLa4KbchEBXkyXcVCyMDHc3rsaHOcYeOOPOSQ5Q6Ta-fvit46gw5uHVySrNCrm7koBTJgOxt_T_JphC4xAMOGgW-o7XUaW_OkU7ajeDtVq3pYhiKOAS4FCgsGRWRMbRnuM6-AKcx3ePW2D2ygy3h9Bgf3Vi-2GDGaJghxRwllZWTI5paeB2hDi2qVwkjG883oKTH6CNgUJoV0Fpk-jks_ZLRPfTyQUKytL-IBOBM9iYaUBdATuCp7hkIXwJakyPsTuw4qgTXZzIuIMzqPaHb4awBHIhQE95wLlDGuesjlSF3XkWzcxPQYYZpFAOxsmMJWD5mnOqjiMxjxRvNbOWBk2dLUNCzcQfzb5CqzDlWOSOhvno-8mgPu8bFaTn3AGZddnXp1Mz9ReP6Lc0UAcLDg2U1Fx3kcpAA%3D%3D)
Now it's a cautionary tale — sky-high taxes, crumbling cities, a mass exodus of families and businesses fleeing for greener pastures. Most of them? They moved to Florida.

And now the Left wants to follow them here.

[**DON'T LET FLORIDA BECOME CALIFORNIA >>**](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=da70678d4d954b22bf04d05dc0d94457&_e=pUQuMl4WOsc59IER2eFenTUR70Djpl93VvQBdyERh5HLHnWDqO8FEl8VCQQfjmxbmnnFMV2ghW4aBFO7TNnJE39J9UbmA7oI0Fxt_VM9yd74VOT30Hv2ttlV7wMaqEZBPb_qqvf-QEVwlugdV7ixKfnsT_-UedfAWM4ZNMxK0-zcMFfcfSoY6HHc2uD5bKhQmZCer-5HbKa5VzbnoMfCHjl54xbuLvIHCueny16o1Ya05O_zZcHopskCqEIpHNHjSdpXhZU6Rb2pBhkUYacJO-qN1lntHRVW6EDPbfi9cj8ooQi4YQ-P8MSOqXSkpiRbc-RkcJ10X_DB4l3hpMsFrngHl0BusM_Mwhk9GTTWS-YbKu63FKU7a9wXu-EG52fixQQaS1qYlWwGwW_yUROai5YAHY4EUzfSxWEm4KFK-B7dathc5jpqqm767XT3ONOMKMQkU8sO3yh1U6sTtcTwNTbgILoQC7EsnCKSgEJ_0OLTLa7R4FcQh4PS4MrdyQlg3O21eHcTajOAQgT57zE32ZUcys7UoF3augAc1BtPmJmakitjl5D9lIgCp3UlWuLog_sXUP7Pj9HOTxUTJPyNA7fC8ZWKwfer8dikE0mstqCqaDvP4skGu8-zGlaW92WJgZQu5d-qZSXdea20UmAMoDKJwVt97Rwp44qtU9nJ7q4MTgQKN5tuNLf17B3JXJdnxTlH3QGJQQf0DixItWUvWw%3D%3D)
The radical Left has made Florida their number one midterm target. _**They are spending millions to flip the Governor's mansion, the Senate seat, and races up and down the ballot — all because they know what taking Florida would mean.**_

It's not just a state to them. [**It's a symbol.**](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=da70678d4d954b22bf04d05dc0d94457&_e=pUQuMl4WOsc59IER2eFenTUR70Djpl93VvQBdyERh5HLHnWDqO8FEl8VCQQfjmxbmnnFMV2ghW4aBFO7TNnJE39J9UbmA7oI0Fxt_VM9yd74VOT30Hv2ttlV7wMaqEZBPb_qqvf-QEVwlugdV7ixKfnsT_-UedfAWM4ZNMxK0-zcMFfcfSoY6HHc2uD5bKhQmZCer-5HbKa5VzbnoMfCHjl54xbuLvIHCueny16o1Ya05O_zZcHopskCqEIpHNHjIpnQ67gcqKZJEOnxjzasua-k0GF0gIYeO-7MsBYOlKcd-ivWR045fSMBtsGzpQmjQ4K2S_k14Fx63ZEJcqCRgVnMnma4ys8qnk26_05TCbAus_gCHVc3gpMxq3ihWU5PwSZqZNl3u1L_oASCsZnh5SJ8_0UujTa2vBQG-rrm3hGuFFYzaetOF0QYcEQ3Zv5wqndUlICCd72qS9Si0qM8WPOLux6oWh4w8MThPbOCxTq3fnatyUhBzQD9w9h9zMSFTexDegt_CDMO1GgNS7pT_TaP5YiNQgHLyrUPCtVAJlcS1SRrgb3RFNjf3ybxbPLX_xmJ0bo99npIJWmqF3PYJsdzHA9my0DpkssJOrbOt6y-RIY6zFDAOTk8wTitcSXCrT8uV5ASGAvCSetIDcHDrzUaKMPTm6KIdEyV9DoEAQnpbPyMoavoXZ6PyZ2Fwb2bh7nTY0Wq5e7DxaUAbZvVGQ%3D%3D)

body:
Why is McConnell Ghosting America?
| | | | |
---
| | | _([Click here to go to petition](https://default.salsalabs.org/T7b58e8da-edc0-4a52-a410-99fd1b29a7ba/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) / Already taken this action? Forward to others! America Deserves Answers?"](https://default.salsalabs.org/T6652b6af-af99-425a-a57b-547816ba9c4c/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** Senator Mitch McConnell has not been seen publicly since mid-June, [after reportedly being rushed to a hospital](https://default.salsalabs.org/T44c990f7-e852-48c2-9b1b-e8cc6b621cae/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)[.](https://default.salsalabs.org/T093dc1c8-a698-470c-9e4a-c97e836f40c4/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) Look, the guy has done all kinds of awful things that have been terrible for America. But we’re not monsters, and we hope he makes a full recovery — and maybe even does something to guarantee all Americans the same kind of apparently excellent health coverage that he has. But he is still a sitting United States senator, and public office requires public accountability. **Kentuckians — and all Americans — deserve a clear update on McConnell’s health, his ability to serve, and when he expects to return to public duties.** No senator, of either party, should be allowed to disappear from public view while voters are told simply to trust that everything is fine. **[Add your name: Senator McConnell and his office should provide a clear public update about his health, capacity to serve, and expected return to public duties.](https://default.salsalabs.org/T3f01e7b7-5965-4679-b1a1-40391b1c55ec/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** And remember to forward this to friends! We are facing real issues that demand real leadership, and that's why I'm reaching out today. **[Will you split a contribution of $5 between Gina Hinojosa's campaign for Governor of Texas and my campaign for Governor of New Mexico?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260711_1_deb.rLbYE8&refcode=em20260711-1539&amount=5&t=2&akid=1539%2E299639%2EFhx8vi)**

Across the country, Democratic governors are leading the fight to lower costs, expand opportunity, protect healthcare, strengthen public schools, and stand up for working families. This November, we have the opportunity to elect two more Democratic governors who are ready to deliver.
I'm running for Governor because New Mexico deserves leadership that will tackle the challenges families face every day and build a future where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.
And in neighboring Texas, my friend Gina Hinojosa is running to fight for strong public schools, affordable healthcare, lower costs, and a state government that works for working people.
Sound familiar?
Peter, the truth is that what happens in Texas affects New Mexico, and vice versa. Our states share a border, but we also share families, workers, businesses, and communities. The decisions made by Texas leaders can have consequences that ripple across our entire region.
For years, Texans have lived under Republican leadership that has put politics ahead of solving problems. Texans deserve better. And New Mexicans deserve a partner next door who is focused on expanding opportunity, protecting freedoms, and delivering real results.
Gina and I believe in the same future for our states: One where working families can get ahead, where every child has access to a great education, where healthcare is within reach, and where the government works for people. _**I know Gina and I will be strong partners in that work.**_
**But this partnership won’t be possible without you, Peter.[If you're ready to help elect governors who will fight for working families across the Southwest, please split a contribution of $5 — or whatever makes sense for you — between our campaigns today. Deb

subject: Too many people were being left behind

body:
Five years ago, I had never run for political office. I was a former Army Captain, a dad to two young kids, and I ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country.
Peter, it’s Governor Wes Moore.
Five years ago, I had never run for political office. I was a former Army Captain, a dad to two young kids, and I ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country.
But I knew more had to be done. While career politicians were saying that everything was great, **I was hearing from folks all across Maryland who were feeling left behind.** So I ran for Governor with a mission to make Maryland a state that serves all our people — and won. (And I’m not done yet!)
**Our mission must continue this year.** I’m running for re-election so we can keep building on the progress we’ve made on jobs, education, public safety, and more. There are tough fights on the horizon, and there’s so much more for us to accomplish together.

name: Andy Beshear
subject: I thought I'd never win this town again
disclaimer_text: Paid for by In This Together PAC
body:
Instead, we got a standing ovation
Peter,

I thought I'd never win Henderson, Kentucky again.

It's a former coal mining community, and by 2019, the county was getting redder. I won there by about 500 votes that year, and I remember thinking — that's probably the last time.

Then, before my reelection in 2023, we landed the cleanest, greenest recycled paper mill in the country, 350 new jobs, paying $40 an hour. At the dedication, the owner spoke and said the one phrase I’d urged him to avoid in coal country: "green jobs." I braced for the reaction.

Instead, folks in Henderson gave him a standing ovation — because a job that pays $40 an hour isn’t green, red or blue. It’s just a good-paying job that allows people to support their families.

That November, I won Henderson County again, with nearly three times as many votes.

**That's not a fluke. That's what happens when you show up, deliver, and let the results speak for themselves. And it's exactly the bet we're making at In This Together PAC — that pragmatic leaders who do the work can win anywhere, even in the places the pundits have written off.**

[_**Will you donate right now to support the next leaders who can win in tough races?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135081268/633044109/1745705010?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_Henderson_260711_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYzE0NmM1Y2MtMzA3ZC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=O0npk0G92v8iwpnlLJ52f67hIJadGBbaYLZFrBInHwI=)

Here's what I've learned, in Henderson and everywhere else: When most Americans wake up in the morning, they're not thinking about that next election. They're thinking about their job and whether they can afford to raise their family. They're thinking about their next doctor’s appointment, the roads they drive, their kids’ school, and whether they feel safe in their community.

We win when we move the needle on those things that lift everyone up and leave no one out.

In This Together PAC exists to back the leaders willing to show up and do the work — in red counties, purple states, and everywhere else the map is supposedly stacked against us.

Henderson didn't change because of a slogan. It changed because people saw what was possible, and we earned their trust one job, one promise kept, at a time. That's the model. Now we need the resources to take it everywhere.

A good chunk of voters already see right through his MAGA branding; they believe he is “out for himself” and does not share their values.

They are tired of the politics of personal wealth. They’re looking for leadership they can trust, someone who understands what it means to work hard, get up before the sun, and put food on the table for our families.

clean_body: | = = Friend, It’s mid-July, and this moment is as close to make-or-break as it gets. In just a year and a half back in office, Trump has moved full steam ahead with his dangerous, extreme, cuckoo agenda. We’ve seen our civil liberties attacked, our public safety degraded, and our systems of due process disregarded. And now we’re embroiled in a dangerous war in Iran. If you think it couldn’t get worse, consider this: If we don’t flip a handful of competitive Senate seats, the Senate will remain a rubber stamp for everything the Trump administration wants to do. = | = I’ve never seen anything like this. This is unbelievable, and we cannot stand for this B.S. Flipping the Senate is our best shot at stopping Trump and holding his corrupt administration accountable, but let me be completely honest with you: It’s going to be one hell of a fight. Trump’s allies are raising truckloads of cash to protect their seats and launch attacks against Democratic champions so they can defend their Senate majority this November. | | Hey Peter, I'm not gonna lie — it's easy to feel the weight of everything right now.

A reckless war with no end in sight. The most corrupt administration in our country's history. Billionaires using the White House to rig contracts and get richer while working families can't afford rent or groceries.

I see it. I feel it too.

But here's what I also see: people showing up anyway. Fighting anyway. Refusing to let this moment define what's possible.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: It's official: We did it.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
This housing bill is proof that progress is possible

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2960%2E4032634%2ESUVy4r)
---
Last night at midnight, my housing bill, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, officially became the law of the land. Double woohoo! Donald Trump refused to sign it. But it didn't matter. Since Congress passed it and he took no action, it automatically went into effect while he was snoozing last night. This fight was never about Donald Trump. It was about whether Congress could act to make life more affordable for working families. And today, the Democrats delivered a new bipartisan law to lower costs. This is the biggest housing law in more than 30 years — a landmark bill that will build more homes, lower housing costs, and help more families achieve the dream of homeownership. [**This victory belongs to everyone who refused to give up. If you're with me in celebrating this huge win for working families today, will you chip in $28 to help us keep this momentum going and keep fighting to get our government to actually do its job?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3706?amount=28&t=8&akid=2960%2E4032634%2ESUVy4r)

---
_If you've saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process automatically:_ |
---
| [DONATE NOW: $3](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3706?t=22&express_lane=true&amount=3&akid=2960%2E4032634%2ESUVy4r)
---

---

---
| [DONATE NOW: $100](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3706?t=18&express_lane=true&amount=100&akid=2960%2E4032634%2ESUVy4r)
---
| [OTHER AMOUNT](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3706?t=20&express_lane=true&akid=2960%2E4032634%2ESUVy4r)
---

---
So here’s what happened. Weeks ago, Republicans and Democrats passed this bill with overwhelming bipartisan support. I’m talking more than 90-percent of lawmakers in Congress voted for this housing affordability bill. Then Donald Trump decided to play politics. For 10 days, he threw a tantrum. Refusing to sign the bill because he wanted to use it as leverage to force Congress to pass his voter suppression bill, the SAVE Act. Trump even dismissed this housing bill as "a yawn." The good news is that the Constitution doesn't give a president a veto by neglect. If Congress is still in session and a president refuses to act on a bill for 10 days, that bill becomes law anyway. So, thanks for nothing, Donald. With the passage of this bill, we’re going to: Build more homes by cutting unnecessary red tape and speeding up construction, giving families more affordable places to live. Expand homeownership by making it easier for working people to qualify for mortgages and buy their first home. Put families ahead of Wall Street by stopping private equity firms from buying up the single-family homes that should belong to people who want to live in them. Today is worth celebrating. But I'm not confusing one victory for the finish line. There’s a whole lot more we need our government to do to actually address the issues that people are struggling with. The good news is that we just proved we CAN get legislation passed that actually meets the moment. We just need to continue to keep up the fight. [**This victory didn't happen by accident. It happened because millions of people refused to give up, organized, spoke out, and demanded action. If you're ready to build on this momentum, will you pitch in $28 today?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3706?amount=28&t=14&akid=2960%2E4032634%2ESUVy4r) Every contribution helps us take on the next fight for working families. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

Today I'm going to answer two questions.
One of the ones I got the most on the campaign trail in Missouri: "Where have all the Democrats gone?"
And probably the question I've gotten the most over the last year, some variation of: "Why doesn't the Republican Party stand up to/distance themselves from/ditch President Trump given his [high disapproval](https://substack.com/redirect/a03d15ae-c6ce-4ff8-bedf-671fa3ceb699?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ratings?" ([Recent polls](https://substack.com/redirect/ab2d2638-5dfb-4264-8575-7744c5a5c8ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reflect just 35% approval and 61% disapproval for the President)
For the second question, people often pose all sorts of theories from cowardice, to apathy, to Republicans simply just believing in the Administration's policies and actions despite polling seeming to show a lot of Americans aren't fans. I'm sure everyone has their own varying shades of personal reasons for supporting the President, but for the Republican Party as a whole, whether they like the President or agree with him isn't nearly as important as one great overriding factor: math.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9sdWNhc2t1bmNlLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.WUvG6lgZybxSrRak_n8WAiTR-dJ8YOxAagkzz0OClrU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=206579342)
Which brings us back to "Where have all the Democrats gone?"
People in Missouri are very interested in this question because up until 2016, Democrats held nearly every statewide elected office in Missouri and now they hold none.
To get a feel for what's happening, let's compare my US Senate election in 2024 (Presidential + Senate year) to 2016, the last time there was both a Presidential and Senate election in the state.
The difference ii percentages is stark. In 2024, I lost my senate election in a wave Republican year by 13.8%, while in 2016, Democratic challenger Jason Kander barely lost his bid for the Senate by just 2.8%.
But looking at the raw vote totals is confusing.
In 2024, I received 1,243,728 votes.
In 2016, Jason got 1,300,200 votes, not even 60,000 more votes than I did.
However...
In 2024, Josh Hawley got 1,651,907 votes.
While in 2016, Roy Blunt received just 1,378,458 votes, nearly 300,000 fewer than Hawley did.
The Democratic votes in the Senate race essentially stayed the same, but I was beaten by 400,000 votes and Jason only lost by 78,000.
In fact, even if I had the _same amount_ of votes in 2024 as Jason had in 2016, and they were taken directly from Hawley's total, I would have still lost by nearly 300,000 votes: 1,595,435 to 1,300,200.
So what gives? If I had close to the same amount of votes as Jason, why were the results so different?
Election numbers can be interpreted in zillions of different ways, but my experience with the electorate and these numbers don't make it seem like all the Democrats are necessarily gone. And it can't be a red population increase swamping Democrats, because Missouri's population only increased by about 150,000 people between 2016 and 2024 (which includes non-voters and kids).
So what is the most likely answer?
It's Donald Trump.
Does anyone remember the early 2010's when Obama was President and pundits everywhere were talking about the [future death of the Republican Party](https://substack.com/redirect/68a37898-de6c-49c1-9042-52bde04f7beb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) due to American demographic changes?
The subtitle for this article is "Where have all the Democrats gone?" Ironically, in 2009, people were asking literally the exact opposite question, like this article that is literally titled "[Where have all the Republicans gone?](https://substack.com/redirect/dc7bb98f-5ec4-49c7-9a62-0d7d0bdf371d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"
The truth is that Donald Trump saved the Republican Party from what many deemed an unavoidable slow death by creating hundreds of thousands of new Republican voters in Missouri and millions more across the country. And these new voters are enthusiastic about it, too (or at least they were in 2020 and 2024 in Missouri).
It's been a massive boon for the Republican Party with real coattails, because since 2016, President Trump has both taken over the Republican Party and also educated all of his voters that that must vote for Republicans in order to support him.
I experienced that on the campaign trail. Missouri used to have a huge amount of ticket splitting, yet over and over again I was told on the by voters that they couldn't stand my opponent and liked me (which was backed up by favorability polling), but that they had to vote Republican in order to support President Trump.
He hasn't just transformed the Republican Party, he has transformed the electorate in a way that the Republican Party desperately needed in order to bounce back from the demographic and other challenges that they didn't have another answer to.
So when you wonder why the Republican party doesn't distance themselves from President Trump, it's important to remember that (like the President says), he IS the Republican Party. He was the miracle they needed to turn what seemed like an insurmountable tide. And if they abandon the new slice of electorate he delivered them, which is generally working class and in a vacuum probably more amenable to liberal than conservative policies, particularly economically, they risk returning to an era where they were staring down a political landscape with no real future.
In the end, the question isn't necessarily where have all the Democrats gone, it's where have all these new Republicans come from? And the answer is the reason they stick by the President no matter what.
Lucas

Peter, as if Iowa's six-week abortion ban wasn't cruel enough, things just got even worse.

**On July 1, a new law took effect requiring abortion medication to be prescribed and dispensed in person,** eliminating the option for eligible patients to receive care through a telehealth appointment and have their medication mailed by an Iowa provider.

Getting an in-person appointment isn't as simple as opponents want you to believe. It can mean taking time off work, driving hours to find a provider, arranging childcare, or waiting weeks for an appointment that's already hard to come by.

That's before you consider that Iowa is already facing physician shortages and the closure of reproductive health clinics across the state. Instead of addressing those problems, politicians have chosen to create yet another barrier between Iowans and the healthcare they need.

Mariannette Miller-Meeks helped pave the way for exactly this moment. She championed Iowa's six-week abortion ban, and she's done nothing to address the provider shortages and clinic closures that are making healthcare less accessible across our state.

[**Enough is enough. Iowans deserve a representative who protects reproductive freedom and believes that medical decisions belong between patients and their doctors — not politicians. That's the kind of representative Christina will be. The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office estimated the bill will cut federal spending on Medicaid and CHIP by over _$1 trillion_ , eliminating coverage for at least _10.5 million people_ by 2034. DesJarlais is a doctor. He knows exactly what happens when people lose healthcare. **He voted for it anyway.**

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Noting our progressive candidates’ astounding victories over long-term
Democratic incumbents Diana DeGette in Denver and Adriano Espaillat in New
York, the New York Times just laid out their list of which Democrats are
next on the chopping block.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260711-1.gF8PYA&refcode=em20260711-38015&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38015%2E1203867%2EnVXqfz ]Screenshot of a headline from the New York Times: "The Incumbent
